title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: genus-0 part of the 'Teichmüller tower/groupoid' (S0 T_{g,ν}). The page enumerates special configurations of marked points on the Riemann sphere. These serve as base points or vertices for a groupoid or cell structure on the moduli spaces M_{0,4} and M_{0,5}. Each configuration is drawn as a map on S^2 whose vertices are the marked points, plus 'cercles marqués', i.e. pinching curves or degeneration circles. For each configuration Grothendieck counts vertices and faces and the number of 'possibilités sur I', i.e. the size of the orbit or number of positions.

(1) M_{0,4}.
(a) The 4 points sit at the vertices of a regular tetrahedron. The map is the complete graph K4 on S^2, with 4 vertices and 4 faces. This is the equianharmonic configuration (cross-ratio e^{±iπ/3}), which has 'deux possibilités'.
(b) Delete one of the three pairs of opposite edges of K4 ('supprimer une des trois paires d'arêtes opposées'). This leaves a 4-cycle on a great circle, with 4 vertices and 2 faces. It is the real or harmonic configuration (4 points on a circle, square-symmetric), with 3 possibilities. These correspond to the 3 cyclic orders up to reversal, i.e. the 3 harmonic points / 3 real arcs of the λ-line.
(c) From (b), add a marked circle separating the points into two adjacent pairs, in 2 ways. The map then has 6 vertices (4 points plus 2 crossings) and 4 faces, with 6 possibilities. These are naturally read as 3 real components × 2 boundary directions, i.e. the 6 real tangential base points 01→, 10→, ... of P^1−{0,1,∞}.
The arrows record incidences: the 2 tetrahedral points, the 3 harmonic points and the 6 degenerate-oriented positions. The S4 action factors through S3 of order 6, giving orbit sizes 2, 3, 6.

(2) M_{0,5}, Z/2 stabilizers. Five points lie on a real circle; there are 12 cyclic orders up to reversal, which are the 12 pentagons of the real locus \bar M_{0,5}(R).
- Type I (D01): two disjoint marked circles crossing the equator. Euler count: V = 5+4 = 9, E = 13, F = 6. The real maximally degenerate stable curve together with a chosen real component gives 12·5 = 60 = (pentagon, vertex).
- Type II (D02): one marked circle. V = 5+2 = 7, F = 4, giving 12·5 = 60 = (pentagon, side).
In both cases 60 = 120/2, the S5-orbit of a configuration with Z/2 symmetry.

Purpose: choosing a canonical system of real/degenerate base points ('points base tangentiels') and their incidences. This would give the vertices of the genus-0 Teichmüller groupoid (Lego), generated in dimensions 1 and 2 by M_{0,4} and M_{0,5}, i.e. the 'pentagon' level. The scribbled sketch on the right is an abandoned picture of such a cell.
errors: The transcription reads '[-3-] faces' for type I. The Euler characteristic forces 6 faces (V=9, E=13), so the figure is presumably a 6 written over or misread. Otherwise the counts check out: 4/2, 6/4, 4/4, 7/4, 60 = 12·5.
'possibilités sur I': I is probably an index (level I) rather than the icosahedron. The bottom labels I and II are the two configuration types; interpretation is uncertain.

ideas.what: Equianharmonic (tetrahedral) and harmonic (square on a great circle) configurations of 4 points as distinguished points of M_{0,4}, with orbit sizes 2 and 3 under S3.
ideas.modern_name: orbifold points of M_{0,4} / anharmonic group

ideas.what: Configurations with a marked (pinching) circle plus a real/cyclic structure, 6 for n=4, as base points.
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses base points for the Teichmüller tower in general terms

ideas.what: Real locus of \bar M_{0,5} tiled by 12 pentagons. Maximal degenerations and boundary edges counted as 12·5 = 60 flags with Z/2 stabilizer.
ideas.modern_name: \bar M_{0,5}(R) as tiling by associahedra K_4 (pentagons)

ideas.what: Using special configurations of genus-0 moduli with their incidences as vertices of the Teichmüller (Lego) groupoid.

missed.claim: Explicit, dated (c. 1978–79) use of real cyclic-order structures on marked points together with degeneration circles. The counts 60 = (pentagon, vertex) and (pentagon, side) amount to the 12-pentagon structure of \bar M_{0,5}(R) and real tangential base points, well before Deligne/Drinfeld/Kapranov/Devadoss.
missed.quote: 12.5 = 60 possibilités pour K (pentagone + sommet) ... 12.5 = 60 poss. point (pentagone + orient.)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority: documents that Grothendieck's Teichmüller-Lego programme already organised base points via the real pentagonal tiling of \bar M_{0,5}. The mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The content (special points of M_{0,4}, pentagons of \bar M_{0,5}(R), tangential base points) is now standard. The early date and explicit flag-counting with real components are a mild historical point, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'deux foci' / 'trois foci' are probably 'deux façons' / 'trois façons' (the number of ways for each arrow).
'supprimer un des trois [pentagones] d'orientées opposées' should probably read 'supprimer une des trois paires d'arêtes opposées' (the crossed-out word being 'paires').
'(trois faces au cercle grand)' is likely '(trois façons, orientées? / ordres cycliques sur cercle grand)'. '6 orientées des cercle grandes' is likely '6 orientations des cercles grands'.
Type I: '[-3-] faces' should be 6 faces by Euler count.
